questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14097284/assets/5d67b2209b622bd26ce7e4ee488ca02208bb120fcd0ab01c602db67da1291dc9.png)

Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ generate the parabola shown above?
questions.worked_solution:
The diagram shows that the parabola is vertical, has its vertex at $(0,0),$ and passes through the point $(6,3).$

The parametric equations of a vertical parabola  that has its vertex at $(0,0)$ are

$$
x=2pt,\,y=p{t}^{2},
$$

where $p$ is constant.

Since the parabola passes through $(6,3),$ we can substitute $x=6$ and $y=3$ into the standard parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

$$
{\begin{aligned}6=2pt \\ 3=p{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the first equation for $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}6 & =2pt \\ 3 & =pt \\ t & =\frac{3}{p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the second equation and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3 & =p{(\frac{3}{p})}^{2} \\ 3 & =p\cdot \frac{9}{{p}^{2}} \\ 3 & =\frac{9}{p} \\ p & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x=2(3)t,\,y=(3){t}^{2},
$$

which simplify to

$$
x=6t,\,y=3{t}^{2}.
$$

questions.problem: Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ generate the horizontal parabola given by the Cartesian equation ${y}^{2}=2x?$
questions.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a horizontal parabola ${y}^{2}=4px$ that has its vertex at $(0,0)$ are

$$
x=p{t}^{2},\,y=2pt,
$$

where $p$ is constant.

Comparing the given Cartesian equation with the general case ${y}^{2}=4px$ and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4px & =2x \\ 4p & =2 \\ p & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x=(\frac{1}{2}){t}^{2},\,y=2(\frac{1}{2})t,
$$

which simplify to

$$
x=\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2},\,y=t.
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the following parabola:

$$
x=3t,\,y=\frac{3}{5}{t}^{2},\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty )
$$

The Cartesian equation of the parabola is

${x}^{2}=$
{{field-1}}.
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's make $t$ the subject of the parametric equations. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}t & =\frac{x}{3},\,{t}^{2}=\frac{5y}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring both sides of the first equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now eliminate the parameter $t$ by substituting the above into the equation ${t}^{2}=\frac{5y}{3}$ and rearranging to find the Cartesian equation of the parabola, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{9} & =\frac{5y}{3} \\ {x}^{2} & =15y\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian equation of the parabola is ${x}^{2}=15y.$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The diagram shows that the parabola is vertical, has its vertex at $(0,0),$ and passes through the point $(4,8).$

The parametric equations of a vertical parabola  that has its vertex at $(0,0)$ are

$$
x = 2pt, \qquad y = pt^2,
$$

where $p$ is constant.

Since the parabola passes through $(4,8),$ we can substitute $x=4$ and $y=8$ into the standard parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

$$
{\begin{aligned}4=2pt \\ 8=p{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the first equation for $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =2pt \\ 2 & =pt \\ t & =\frac{2}{p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the second equation and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}8 & =p{(\frac{2}{p})}^{2} \\ 8 & =p\cdot \frac{4}{{p}^{2}} \\ 8 & =\frac{4}{p} \\ p & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x = 2\left(\dfrac 12 \right)t, \qquad y = \left(\dfrac 12 \right)t^2 ,
$$

which simplify to

$$
x = t, \qquad y = \dfrac 12 t^2 .
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Find the Cartesian equation of the parabola defined by the parametric equations

$$
x = 2t^2, \qquad y = 4t, \qquad t\in(-\infty,\infty).
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, let's make $t$ the subject of the parametric equations. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & =\frac{x}{2},\,t=\frac{y}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring both sides of the second equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & =\frac{{y}^{2}}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now eliminate the parameter $t$ by substituting the above into the equation $t^2 = \dfrac{x}{2}$ and rearranging to find the Cartesian equation of the parabola, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{y}^{2}}{16} & =\frac{x}{2} \\ {y}^{2} & =8x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian equation of the parabola is $y^2 = 8x.$
